fact_check_verdict: PASS WITH CONDITIONS. Alaska release November 19th verified verbatim (ordered at the urging of the coalition, auction planned December 1st, Mills quotes). NY AG October 14th: 40 AGs incl DC, 20M monthly users and 2M self-declared under 18 accounts (NY figures), data trains its AI. Docket facts secondary only (KSL/Reuters, Bloomberg Law, KQED, PPC Land, KIMT); no primary docket reachable. Do not say: Chapter 11 from the state release, ombudsman can block, sale halted, 40 states, 2 million children, Alaska led, Disney buying chats, 163 million users, backer's name.

claims.spoken: Character.AI filed for bankruptcy in October.
claims.verbatim_source: Paraphrase from fetch, not a quotation: Reuters via KSL reports Character.AI filed for bankruptcy late on Monday, October 12th, 2026, with first-day papers the next day.
requires: say October or October 12th, never October 13th

claims.spoken: Character.AI lets people talk with AI characters.
claims.verbatim_source: "Character.AI allows users to interact with AI-generated characters, including fictional personalities and chatbots posing as therapists, psychologists, and other trusted professionals."

claims.spoken: Some of its chatbots posed as therapists.
claims.verbatim_source: "chatbots posing as therapists, psychologists, and other trusted professionals."
requires: attribute to the Alaska Department of Law or the state attorneys general

claims.spoken: It has about twelve million monthly users, per its filings.
claims.verbatim_source: Paraphrase from fetch, not a quotation: KQED reports roughly 12 million monthly users according to the company's legal filings; Reuters via KSL says about 12 million active users.
requires: say per its filings or per the company

claims.spoken: New York's attorney general put it above twenty million monthly users, including more than two million accounts self-declared as under eighteen.
claims.verbatim_source: "The platform has more than 20 million monthly users, including more than two million accounts registered to users self-declared as under 18."
requires: say self-declared, never 2 million children
attribute to the New York attorney general

claims.spoken: It collects private chats, voice calls and mental health disclosures.
claims.on_screen: PRIVATE CHATS · VOICE CALLS · MENTAL HEALTH
claims.verbatim_source: "Character.AI collects sensitive user information, including private chats and voice calls, mental health disclosures, ages, and identifying device data."
requires: attribute to the attorneys general

claims.spoken: It uses that information to train its AI, the attorneys general said.
claims.on_screen: USED TO TRAIN ITS AI · PER THE AGS
claims.verbatim_source: "The company uses this information to generate revenue and train its AI, and the data could be transferred to a new owner through bankruptcy."
requires: attribute to the attorneys general

claims.spoken: The data could pass to a new owner through bankruptcy.
claims.on_screen: COULD TRANSFER TO A NEW OWNER
claims.verbatim_source: "the data could be transferred to a new owner through bankruptcy."

claims.spoken: The company plans to auction it on December 1st.
claims.verbatim_source: "...which the company plans to auction off on December 1, 2026."
requires: say plans or scheduled, never will be sold

claims.spoken: A starting bid of ten million dollars covers the app, its AI models, user accounts and chat content.
claims.on_screen: $10M STARTING BID · APP · MODELS · ACCOUNTS · CHATS
claims.verbatim_source: Paraphrase from fetch, not a quotation: Bloomberg Law reports Smirks & Pangs Acquisition LLC is the starting bidder at $10 million for the website, mobile apps, finished and unfinished AI models, and user accounts and chat content.
requires: never say Disney is buying the chats

claims.spoken: The starting bidder is a company formed the day before the filing that disclosed its bid, and its backer isn't public.
claims.on_screen: FORMED NOV 13TH · BID FILED NOV 14TH · BACKER NOT PUBLIC
claims.verbatim_source: Paraphrase from fetch, not a quotation: Bloomberg Law says Smirks & Pangs was formed November 13th and the bid disclosed in a November 14th filing; the company asked the court to keep the backer confidential (Bloomberg Law and PPC Land, November 20th).
requires: never name or guess the backer

claims.spoken: Disney bid twenty million dollars for a license to the technology, not the chats.
claims.on_screen: DISNEY · $20M · TECH LICENSE · NOT THE CHATS
claims.verbatim_source: Paraphrase from fetch, not a quotation: Reuters via KSL reports Disney is the stalking-horse bidder at $20 million for a nonexclusive, perpetual license to Character.AI's intellectual property; the user data sits in the separate $10 million bid.

claims.spoken: In October Alaska joined a bipartisan coalition of attorneys general.
claims.verbatim_source: "In October, Alaska joined a bipartisan coalition of state attorneys general in raising concerns about Character.AI's privacy and safety practices."
requires: say joined, never led

claims.spoken: New York led it, with thirty nine other attorneys general.
claims.verbatim_source: "New York Attorney General Letitia James and a bipartisan coalition of 39 other attorneys general today warned that Character.AI should not be sold without strong protections for the millions of people..."
requires: say attorneys general, never 40 states

claims.spoken: At the coalition's urging, the court ordered a consumer privacy ombudsman.
claims.verbatim_source: "At the urging of the coalition, the bankruptcy court ordered the appointment of a Consumer Privacy Ombudsman to review the potential sale of users' private conversations and personal information and recommend safeguards to the court before the sale of the company's assets."
requires: attribute the urging to the Alaska Department of Law

claims.spoken: The ombudsman reviews the sale of users' private conversations and recommends safeguards to the court.
claims.verbatim_source: "review the potential sale of users' private conversations and personal information and recommend safeguards to the court"

claims.spoken: The ombudsman advises. The court decides.
claims.on_screen: THE OMBUDSMAN ADVISES · THE COURT DECIDES
claims.verbatim_source: 11 U.S.C. 332(b): the ombudsman "shall provide to the court information to assist the court in its consideration of the facts, circumstances, and conditions of the proposed sale"; 363(b)(1)(B): the court approves such sale after appointment of the ombudsman and notice and a hearing.
requires: never say the ombudsman can block or veto the sale

claims.spoken: By law the ombudsman weighs the privacy policy, what users could lose or gain, and alternatives that would cut the losses.
claims.on_screen: PRIVACY POLICY · LOSSES OR GAINS · ALTERNATIVES
claims.verbatim_source: 11 U.S.C. 332(b): information may include "(1) the debtor's privacy policy; (2) the potential losses or gains of privacy to consumers ... (4) the potential alternatives that would mitigate potential privacy losses or potential costs to consumers."

claims.spoken: The U.S. Trustee named Lucy Thomson, a data privacy expert.
claims.verbatim_source: Paraphrase from fetch, not a quotation: PPC Land reports the US Trustee appointed Lucy L. Thomson by a November 18th notice; KIMT: "The United States Trustee selected data privacy expert Lucy Thompson to fill that role." (KIMT misspells the surname.)
requires: spell Thomson
the Trustee appointed her, not the judge

claims.spoken: Mills said children and families should not have to worry their private conversations can be sold to the highest bidder.
claims.on_screen: "SOLD TO THE HIGHEST BIDDER" · ACTING AG CORI MILLS
claims.verbatim_source: "Children and families should not have to worry that their private conversations can be sold to the highest bidder," said Acting Attorney General Mills.
requires: attribute to Acting Attorney General Cori Mills

claims.spoken: Mills said that responsibility does not disappear when a company files for bankruptcy.
claims.verbatim_source: "Companies have a responsibility to protect the information they collect, and that responsibility does not disappear when they file for bankruptcy."
requires: attribute to Mills

claims.spoken: The state says the company's limits on minors are voluntary and incomplete, and a future buyer could reverse them.
claims.on_screen: LIMITS ON MINORS · VOLUNTARY · COULD BE REVERSED
claims.verbatim_source: "Although Character.AI has voluntarily restricted minors' access to certain chatbot features, ... these measures are voluntary, incomplete, and could be circumvented or reversed by a future buyer."
requires: attribute to the state, it is an argument not a finding

claims.spoken: The investigations followed a twenty twenty four wrongful death lawsuit.
claims.verbatim_source: Alaska: "a 2024 wrongful death lawsuit alleging that the company's chatbots encouraged a child's suicidal thoughts"; NY: "Attorney General James and several other attorneys general began investigating Character.AI after a 2024 wrongful death lawsuit..."
requires: say alleging, never name the plaintiff
several attorneys general investigated, not every coalition state

claims.spoken: The company cited legal costs and losses it couldn't fund.
claims.verbatim_source: Paraphrase from fetch, not a quotation: KQED reports CEO Colin Adams' sworn declaration cited high legal costs, difficulty becoming profitable and investors' concern over litigation; Reuters via KSL says it has never been profitable.
requires: lawsuits allege, never that harm happened

claims.spoken: Character.AI told the court its privacy policy already allowed the sale.
claims.on_screen: "POLICY ALREADY PERMITTED THE SALE" · PER THE COMPANY
claims.verbatim_source: PPC Land reports the company told the court its policy as in force on the petition date "already permitted the sale and transfer of user data."
requires: attribute to the company's filing, single source PPC Land

claims.spoken: Any sale still needs the court's approval after a hearing.
claims.verbatim_source: 11 U.S.C. 363(b)(1)(B): "after notice and a hearing, the court approves such sale"; PPC Land lists a sale hearing after the December 1st auction.

claims.spoken: The ombudsman can't disclose the personal information it reviews.
claims.verbatim_source: 11 U.S.C. 332(c): an ombudsman "may not disclose personally identifiable information obtained by the ombudsman under this title" (statute text per validator; confirm before quoting on screen).

claims.spoken: Mills said she's pleased the court took the step.
claims.verbatim_source: "I'm pleased the court has taken this important step to protect consumers."

cut.claim: about 163 million current and past users
bid deadline November 24th, sale hearing December 3rd to 4th
ombudsman $650 an hour, report due November 26th
cut.why: PPC only, date is PPC calculation
